title: Testimony and Witness
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Testimony and witness means that God uses restored lives to display His mercy and point others to Jesus Christ. A testimony is not self-promotion, but a truthful witness to the grace and power of God.
summary: Testimony and witness means that God uses restored lives to display His mercy and point others to Jesus Christ. A testimony is not self-promotion, but a truthful witness to the grace and power of God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the center of every faithful testimony. Believers do not merely tell how life improved; they bear witness to the Savior who forgives, restores, delivers, and gives new life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God often turns mercy received into witness shared. Those who have been forgiven, restored, delivered, or sustained can tell others what the Lord has done.

A testimony should glorify Christ, not the past sin, the personality of the speaker, or dramatic details. The focus is the mercy, truth, and power of God.

Witness is not limited to those with dramatic stories. Every believer has a testimony of grace. Some testify to deliverance from visible bondage; others testify to God’s quiet faithfulness, preservation, repentance, and hope.

Testimony should be joined with the Gospel. Changed lives are powerful, but the message must point clearly to Christ’s death, resurrection, repentance, faith, and saving grace.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Restored people may wonder whether their past disqualifies them from usefulness. This doctrine says God can use redeemed stories to point others to Christ.

It also protects testimony from becoming performance. The goal is not to impress people with darkness or transformation, but to make much of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Share what God has done with humility, wisdom, and Gospel clarity. Do not glorify your past or hide Christ behind your story. Let your life and words point others to the Savior who forgives, restores, and gives hope.
